steps.label: The claim: superposition = free parallel search
steps.sub: n qubits in superposition supposedly explore all 2ⁿ answers simultaneously

steps.label: True: uniform superposition has nonzero amplitude everywhere
steps.sub: All 2ⁿ basis states really do carry nonzero amplitude at once

steps.label: False: you can't just 'read off' the right one
steps.sub: Measurement gives one random string — no better than guessing

steps.label: Superposition alone buys zero advantage at readout
steps.sub: Equal amplitudes measured just give a uniformly random result

steps.label: Amplitudes are complex — they combine
steps.sub: They can reinforce (constructive) or cancel (destructive) before measurement

steps.label: Good algorithms reinforce the correct answer
steps.sub: A specific gate sequence grows the right amplitude across several steps

steps.label: ...and drive wrong answers toward cancellation
steps.sub: Incorrect outcomes' amplitude shrinks toward zero

steps.label: Only then do you measure
steps.sub: Probability mass is now concentrated enough for a reliable readout

steps.label: Shor's algorithm: exponential speedup for factoring
steps.sub: Exploits periodicity via the quantum Fourier transform

steps.label: Grover's algorithm: quadratic speedup for search
steps.sub: √N queries instead of N — real, provably optimal, far from exponential

steps.label: Neither is 'classical plus superposition'
steps.sub: Each is a distinct, engineered construction exploiting problem structure

steps.label: More qubits with the wrong algorithm buys nothing
steps.sub: The speedup lives in the interference structure, not in qubit count
